name: What is the difference between mitered window casing and butt-joint casing?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between mitered window casing and butt-joint casing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mitered casing joins the side and top trim at 45-degree angles, creating a uniform border around the window. Butt-joint casing (common in Craftsman and modern designs) positions vertical side casings flat against a wider top header piece and a bottom stool or apron. Mitered joints deliver a classic picture-frame look but require extreme precision and tight nailing to prevent corner separation when indoor temperatures shift. Butt-joint designs are sturdier against wood movement, fit thicker head moldings easily, and offer a clean, substantial profile.
acceptedAnswer.description: Mitered casing connects trim at 45-degree angles, while butt-joint casing squares vertical side legs against a distinct top header and bottom sill.
